propositions.claim: The Federal Register of Wednesday 26 Nov 1941 (Volume 6, Number 229, p. 5987) prints the order as No. 8947 under the heading Executive Order.
propositions.quote: EXECUTIVE ORDER / Revocation of Executive Order No. 1474 of February 16, 1912, Withdrawing Public Land / COLORADO

propositions.claim: The order's only operative sentence revokes EO 1474 by its own words.
propositions.quote: Executive Order No. 1474 of February 16, 1912, withdrawing lot 2, sec. 1, T. 27 S., R. 71 W., Sixth Principal Meridian, Colorado, for use by the Forest Service as the Malachite Administrative Site in connection with the administration of the San Isabel National Forest, is hereby revoked.

propositions.claim: The order was signed on 24 November 1941, the date the revocation took effect, since the text states no later effective date.
propositions.quote: FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT THE WHITE HOUSE, November 24, 1941.

propositions.claim: The whole text is one sentence resting on the 1910 withdrawal act, with no savings clause, condition or continuing command.
propositions.quote: By virtue of the authority vested in me by the act of June 25, 1910, 36 Stat. 847 (U.S.C., title 43, sec. 141), Executive Order No. 1474 of February 16, 1912 ... is hereby revoked.

review.conclusion_reason: The transcription supports the spent-on-issue interpretation, but an accepted original was not verified. The formal-status search finding also cannot be independently established from the cited sources; the slice's empty later-instrument list is only a lead. This does not establish that the worker's conclusion is false.

verdicts.reason: The cited govinfo PDF repeatedly failed to load; its heading, order number, page and filing notation could not be checked.
The held APP transcription contains the quoted revocation sentence, but the cited official printing could not be opened to confirm it.
The held transcription gives November 24, 1941 and contains no later effective date, but the cited official printing was inaccessible.

The held transcription has one operative sentence with the stated statutory authority and no savings clause, condition or continuing command; completeness against the cited original remains unverified.
The quotation appears verbatim in the named held file, but the claimed match to the Federal Register cannot be confirmed without reading that printing.
